title: Quasi-isometry invariance of continuous regular-representation Lp cohomology for unimodular locally compact second-countable groups
author: Marc Bourdon; Bertrand Rémy
work: Quasi-isometric invariance of continuous group $L^p$-cohomology, and first applications to vanishings
source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue 3 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/ahl.61
difficulty_reason: The authored proof identifies continuous group cohomology with a measurable relatively injective resolution, constructs invariant representatives using an equivariant conull model, and equates local-integrability and asymptotic cochain topologies to import coarse invariance. This topological homological comparison exceeds ordinary qualifying exams.

primary_locator.selected_hypotheses: both locally compact second-countable groups unimodular, 1<p<infinity, compatible left-invariant proper metrics
primary_locator.required_core: complete author relative-injective resolution, second equivariant conull invariant-representative construction, cochain topology comparison

source_scope_note: The selected problem is Theorem 1.1/Corollary 3.7 restricted to both groups unimodular, locally compact and second countable, with compatible left-invariant proper metrics and 1<p<infinity. It concerns ordinary and reduced continuous right-regular Lp cohomology and depends only on the bounded-perturbation class of the quasi-isometry. The complete author body retains all local relatively injective resolution, equivariant conull second invariant-representative construction and cochain-seminorm comparison. The first differentiation-based construction and general nonunimodular and Lie-group application assertions are unchanged unselected context; named coarse invariance and foundational resolution results remain explicit references.
